# What the proof run on SEEN-008 established, and the three defects it found

Criterion 1's evidence lives in SEEN-008's journal, on its own branch, so the facts are transcribed here
where this ticket's gate can read them. SEEN-008 is "Create trade-record schema v1 with tenant_id and RLS
on every table", 5 points and not at most 2, which is the deviation Ruud recorded when he chose it as the
proof on 27 September 2026.

**The run, driven by `harness run` at every step.** Clarify passed with `clarified` at 0.86 and `risk` high
at 0.84; solution passed at 0.62 with `touches_billing_or_policy_gate` no by 0.51 to 0.49, which is close
enough to be worth recording; the route sent all three slices to opus at high effort **by rule**, not by
Jev, because a slice carrying a migration and RLS policies is not Jev's to answer. Three slices, each
worked by `seen-implementer`, RED and GREEN at records 8 and 9, 11 and 12, 14 and 15, every check declaring
`--model opus --agent seen-implementer`. Coverage 17, regression 18, tdd gate 19, triage 20 at depth full
with all five criteria evidenced, then `seen-reviewer` in its own context. **No stop from clarify to
review.** The loop named the next action and its exact arguments at every step and the session executed
it; nothing in the harness launched a model.

**The review returned it, which is the run working rather than failing.** `seen-reviewer` verified all five
criteria against the database rather than against the journal's account of them, and returned the ticket on
three high findings outside the criteria, each reproduced by execution in a rolled-back transaction: an
authenticated member of a tenant could delete its tenant row and the cascade erased the whole trade record
and every audit event through the one branch the append-only trigger permits; authenticated could insert a
compensation settlement line of 999900 cents and a claim marked credited, which is CLAUDE.md's ground rule
about billable events broken directly; and the four database tests that were the entire evidence for four
of the five criteria sat behind a script no CI job, turbo task or root script invoked. All three are now
closed, at records 23 and 24, with `anon` holding nothing on all 29 tables and `authenticated` holding
select only, measured from `relacl` rather than asserted.

**Three defects in the harness itself, found by running it rather than by reading it.** This is what the
fourth return amends the plan for, on Ruud's authority, 27 September 2026.

1. `harness/guard.py:125-128` treats "the plan exists but nothing is accepted yet" and "every slice in it is
   already done" as one state and allows every path in both. So once a ticket's last slice is done the guard
   stops guarding, which is exactly the phase after a return from review, when rework happens and when a
   session is most likely to touch a file no slice named. On SEEN-008 `guard supabase/migrations/...`
   answered `allowed: true`, rule `no-slice-plan`, while `status --brief` said three of three slices were
   done.
2. `harness/guard.py:131` is `relative not in entry['files']`, an exact string match, so a slice that names
   the directory `supabase/migrations` cannot authorise a file inside it: nobody can name a migration's
   timestamped filename in advance. All three of SEEN-008's slices were refused and all three wrote their
   migration through a shell, which the PreToolUse hook does not match. Recorded at records 10, 13 and 16 of
   that journal. The two defects are opposite failures of the same rule: one refuses what the plan allows,
   the other allows what no plan mentions.
3. `harness/coverage.py:19-20` builds `DEFAULT_COMMAND` as `pnpm --filter @seen/core test -- --coverage.enabled
   --coverage.reporter=json-summary`. pnpm forwards the literal `--`, so vitest parks the flags after it and
   never enables coverage, and the gate then reads `packages/core/coverage/coverage-summary.json`, which
   nothing rewrote: after a run it was still the file dated 23 September. So "coverage that fell is refused"
   has not been true, and every coverage check in this session, including this ticket's own at records 17,
   25 and 34, compared a stale figure against the baseline. It is the one of the three that makes the
   harness report a control it does not have.

**Four returns, which is past this ticket's own thrashing threshold, and the record should say why.** Three
were criterion 1 refusing to be evidenced, and the fourth is this deliberate amendment. None was a defect
in the code the ticket delivered. The first return also bought something real: it found that `question_open`
was reading the clarify draft's list rather than a recorded decision below its threshold, and that nothing
read CI at all.
